fred-us-cpi-2026-08-12.standing: The monthly consumer price index from the US Bureau of Labor Statistics, the headline measure of how fast prices are rising across the American economy. It sets the terms for Federal Reserve policy and reprices bonds, currencies and equities on release.
fred-us-cpi-2026-08-12.recent: The Fed held rates at 350-375 basis points on July 29, citing elevated inflation, and this is the first CPI print since. Fuel is the live channel: US diesel costs $5.36 a gallon, and the dollar has fallen to its weakest since May. The release will show how much of that war premium has reached consumer prices.

fred-us-ppi-2026-08-13.standing: The Bureau of Labor Statistics' producer price index, released monthly, measures what US producers receive for their output. It is read as an early signal of cost pressure moving through supply chains toward consumer prices.
fred-us-ppi-2026-08-13.recent: The Bureau of Labor Statistics reports US PPI on 13 August. The release will set the month's reading on producer-level cost pressure ahead of consumer prices.

fred-us-retail-sales-2026-08-14.standing: The Census Bureau's monthly report on receipts at US retail and food-service businesses, released mid-month for the month before. It is the earliest broad read on consumer spending, which drives most of the US economy, and it moves rate expectations and the dollar.
fred-us-retail-sales-2026-08-14.recent: The Census Bureau reports US retail sales on 14 August. The release will settle how much of the quarter's consumer spending held up.

ecb-2026-09.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which sets interest rates for the twenty countries using the euro. Its decisions transmit to borrowing costs across the bloc and to the euro's value against every other major currency.
ecb-2026-09.recent: The decision follows a run of central bank holds: the Bank of England kept rates at 3.75% with three of nine policymakers dissenting for a rise, the Bank of Japan held at 1% while warning underlying inflation exceeds its 2% target, and the US Fed held steady citing elevated inflation. The dollar has since fallen to its lowest level since May.

fomc-2026-09.standing: The Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee, which meets eight times a year to set the target range for overnight bank lending. Its decisions move the cost of borrowing across the dollar economy and every asset priced against it.
fomc-2026-09.recent: The Fed held at 350-375 basis points in July, citing elevated inflation, after investors had priced a hike. Since then the dollar has fallen to its weakest since May, and Trump has renewed his bid to remove Cook, reviving the fight over Fed independence. This meeting settles whether the fuel-led inflation of the summer changes the rate.

boe-2026-09.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, which meets eight times a year to set Bank Rate. Its decision sets the floor for UK borrowing costs, feeding through to mortgages, gilt yields and sterling.
boe-2026-09.recent: The committee held at 3.75% on 30 July with three of nine voting to raise, a split that leaves the next meeting genuinely open. That hold was framed as waiting to see the impact of the Iran war on supply; UK house prices rose 0.1% in July as buyers stayed cautious on rates.

boj-2026-09.standing: Japan's central bank, whose policy board meets eight times a year to set the short-term policy rate. Its decisions set the price of the world's cheapest major funding currency, and move the yen, Japanese government bonds, and global carry trades.

uk-cpi-2026-10.standing: The Office for National Statistics' monthly measure of UK consumer prices, released mid-month for the preceding month. It sets the reference point for Bank of England rate decisions, index-linked gilts, and a range of benefits and contracts uprated by inflation.
uk-cpi-2026-10.recent: The Office for National Statistics reports September consumer price inflation on 21 October. The release will settle where UK price growth stands going into the Bank of England's autumn decisions.

fomc-2026-10.standing: The rate-setting committee of the US Federal Reserve, which meets eight times a year to set the target range for overnight bank lending. Its decisions set the price of dollar credit worldwide, moving currencies, sovereign borrowing costs and every asset priced in dollars.
fomc-2026-10.recent: The Fed held at 350-375 basis points in July, citing elevated inflation, after investors had priced a hike and Citadel bet on one. Since then the dollar has fallen to its weakest since May with a hike in doubt, and Trump has moved again to fire Cook, reviving the fight over Fed independence.

ecb-2026-10.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which sets policy rates for the euro area on a roughly six-week cycle. Its decisions set the cost of credit across the currency union and anchor pricing for euro-denominated debt and assets.
ecb-2026-10.recent: The decision closes a season in which major central banks stayed put and split while doing so: the Bank of England held at 3.75% with three of nine policymakers voting to raise, the Bank of Japan held at 1% while warning underlying inflation is exceeding its 2% target, and the US Fed held citing elevated inflation.

boj-2026-10.standing: Japan's central bank sets short-term policy rates and buys government bonds, meeting eight times a year. Because Japan is the world's largest creditor nation, its rate decisions move global bond yields and the borrowing costs of carry trades funded in yen.
boj-2026-10.recent: The Bank of Japan held rates at 1% on July 31 while warning of underlying inflation exceeding its 2% target, and Tokyo sold dollars for yen hours before the decision. Japan then confirmed a historic joint yen intervention with the US, which pushed the dollar to a one-month low. This meeting will settle whether the rate stays behind the currency defence.

boe-2026-11.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, which meets eight times a year to set Bank Rate. Its decisions set the cost of borrowing across the UK economy, feeding through to mortgages, sterling and gilt yields.
boe-2026-11.recent: The committee held at 3.75% on 30 July with three of nine members voting to raise, and cited the impact of the Iran war as a reason to wait. UK house prices rose 0.1% in July as buyers stayed cautious on rates. This meeting will settle whether that dissenting bloc has grown.
